outcome: A copy has the copiable values of the original (not its counters, status or type-changing effects) and, for a stack object, its mode, targets, X and kicker choices.
A copy has the original's color and exactly one set of the original's abilities.
Changing the original's copiable values after it was copied leaves the copy unchanged.
A static copy effect fixes the copiable values it grants at the moment it first applies.
An object copying a copy gets the copy's copiable values, and a face-down copier stays face down while its face-up values change.
A permanent that becomes a copy of another object while on the battlefield triggers no enters or leaves abilities and keeps its noncopy effects.
An object entering as a copy applies the copied enters-with replacement effects and its copied enters triggers fire.
Choices made for the copied permanent are not copied; the copy's controller makes its own as-enters choices.
note: The new choice is a decision; the non-copying of the old choice is the observable outcome.

outcome: Copied linked abilities are linked only to each other on the copy.
A copy of a double-faced or melded permanent takes the copiable values of the face currently up.
A token copy of a double-faced object has both faces and enters with the same face up as the original.

note: Introduces the sub-rules on exceptions; each carries its own outcome.

outcome: An ability a copy effect grants becomes part of the copy's copiable values and is copied by later copies.
A characteristic modified by a copy effect keeps the modified value in the copy's copiable values.
A characteristic the copy effect does not copy keeps the copying object's original value.
A characteristic-defining ability for a characteristic the copy effect overrides is not copied, except for in-addition-to type exceptions.
An additional-effect exception of a copy effect does not happen if another copy effect is applied afterwards.
A conditional exception of a copy effect applies only if the resulting permanent has the stated characteristics.
A triggered ability linked to a copy-effect replacement does not trigger if another copy effect is applied afterwards.
Copying a spell or ability puts a copy on the stack with the original's modes, targets, X and costs, controlled by the copier, and it is not cast or activated.
A copy of a spell outside the stack, or a copy of a card outside the stack or battlefield, ceases to exist.
A copy of an ability has the same source as the original and refers to that source object.
A copy whose controller may choose new targets keeps unchanged targets even if illegal, and any changed targets must be legal.
note: The choosing is a decision; the legality constraint on the resulting targets is observable.

outcome: A copy is created for each player or object that is a legal target for every instance of target, and none for others.
A copy with a specified new target is created only if that target is legal for every instance of target.
A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token permanent as it resolves.
A copy of a double-faced permanent spell is double-faced, keeps the original's face up, and resolves into a double-faced token.
An effect that refers to a permanent by name still tracks that permanent after it changes name or becomes a copy.
A copy of an object cast by an effect is created in the object's zone, becomes a spell on the stack, and can resolve or be countered.

note: Choosing individually whether to cast each copy is a player's choice.

outcome: The effect creates a copy of the named card with Oracle characteristics outside the game.
The effect creates a copy of the noted card using its characteristics as it last existed in the graveyard.
note: Magar of the Magic Strings only.
